transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-12 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~41 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Ivy (Redwood PD), Lena (SableGrid), Daniel (SableGrid Infra), Ravi (SableGrid GPU Solutions), Priya (SableGrid BD)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we're excited to chat with SableGrid today. quick intros from our side, I'm Maya, AE on partnerships, Samir is our SE who will run the tech bits, and Ivy from product will tag on go-to-market questions.
[00:12] Lena (SableGrid): Hi all, lena here, happy to be here. Quick intro: SableGrid is a regional cloud specializing in GPU tenancy, we sell dedicated pods and managed clusters to ISVs. With us today is Daniel and Ravi.
[00:25] Daniel (SableGrid): yep hey, thanks for the invite.
[00:30] Samir (Redwood): great, quick agenda: partner intro, fleet and infra details, compatibility questions (VPC, KMS, model packaging), then next steps/benchmarks. does that work?
[00:38] Priya (SableGrid): sounds good.
[00:42] Maya (Redwood): cool. to set context, Redwood provides inference runtime across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — our customers care about predictable latency and unit cost. we also have a partner program covering reseller and infra integrations.
[00:58] Ravi (SableGrid): nice — can you give a quick summary of the deployment modes? sometimes our customers ask whether they should use your hosted API vs a dedicated pool on our infra.
[01:10] Maya (Redwood): totally. hosted api is simplest, reserved/dedicated is for committed capacity with SLA, and private gives you VPC or on-prem control plane for regulated workloads. typical trade-offs: hosted is fastest to ship, dedicated gives predictability; private is for data residency and stricter compliance.
[01:35] Daniel (SableGrid): our main ask is: how easy is it to run Redwood on top of our hardware? we have A100 80GB with NVLink and some H100 preorders. also curious about continuous batching and kernel selection — will Redwood adapt?
[01:50] Samir (Redwood): yes, our runtime picks kernels based on model shape and hardware; we support quantized variants. NVLink topologies help with large-context KV cache. quick note: sometimes model names/ops can be mis-transcribed in older docs but in practice we run micro-benchmarks to validate.
[02:10] Lena (SableGrid): ok, can you share a list of tech requirements? network, ports, KMS?
[02:18] Samir (Redwood): high level: control plane (we can run a customer-managed control plane), agent nodes that reach out to the control plane over TLS, KMS integration for keys (we support common KMS/HSM APIs), and optional private S3 for model storage. We prefer a straightforward outbound-only pattern for agents but can do inbound with a VPN.
[02:40] Priya (SableGrid): commercial question — how do partner margins work if we resell dedicated capacity?
[02:47] Maya (Redwood): we have a partner pricing tier for infra partners with rev-share or discounted committed capacity; specifics depend on commit. i'll send the partner pack after this call.
[03:00] Daniel (SableGrid): on the tech side, we often run cluster-level autoscaling and use Kubernetes; can Redwood runtime be containerized?
[03:10] Samir (Redwood): yes, we have a dockerized runtime and helm charts for k8s deployment; we also provide an operator for autoscaling and GPU scheduling. caveat: some performance tuning is required for kernel choices and CUDA versions.
[03:30] Ravi (SableGrid): what about model onboarding? do you expect us to host models or use Redwood's model catalog?
[03:38] Ivy (Redwood): flexible — customers can pin curated open models from our catalog, or bring their own model bundles. for private deployments, model artifacts typically live in customer-managed storage and we point the runtime at them.
[03:55] Lena (SableGrid): security — SOC2 and audit logs? our enterprise customers demand audit trails and SSO.
[04:04] Maya (Redwood): we support SSO/SAML, per-route RBAC, and audit logging. we also integrate with KMS for envelope encryption. we can share our SOC2 cert and architecture notes — you'll get those in the security pack.
[04:18] Priya (SableGrid): good. a couple of customers use CoreWeave and Paperspace — want to understand differentiation vs Lambda/managed clouds.
[04:26] Maya (Redwood): differentiation is our production-first tooling: cost controls (batching, quant profiles), rollout tooling, and a single API surface across hosted/dedicated/private. that'll matter for ISVs who want predictable unit economics.
[04:45] Daniel (SableGrid): on the benchmark piece, can Redwood's test harness run on our infra to measure p99 latency and cost per 1k tokens?
[04:55] Samir (Redwood): yes, we'll provide a small harness and sample prompts. ideally we'll run a 10k request sample across 8/16-token windows and 4k/8k context to see perf and KV cache effectiveness.
[05:10] Ravi (SableGrid): we also want to test multi-tenancy isolation — we carve pods for customers and need to ensure noisy-neighbor protection.
[05:18] Samir (Redwood): we've got admission controls and cgroups integrations; we'll include suggestions for pod sizing and padding.
[05:30] Lena (SableGrid): go-to-market — we want to know how referrals and co-selling would work. do you have partner-marketing assets?
[05:38] Ivy (Redwood): yes, partner co-marketing templates, case study frameworks, and referral credit. we'll share the partner guide in that pack.
[05:48] Priya (SableGrid): timeline — some prospects want pilots in 6-8 weeks. is that feasible?
[05:55] Maya (Redwood): pilot in 6-8 weeks is realistic: quick benchmark in week 1-2, pilot setup in week 3-6, iterate on perf and cost.
[06:06] Daniel (SableGrid): any blockers around CUDA versions or specific driver requirements?
[06:12] Samir (Redwood): we support CUDA 11.x and 12.x but certain quant kernels prefer 12.x; we'll send recommended driver/kernel matrix.
[06:22] Maya (Redwood): quick note on pricing — we price per-token for hosted, and for dedicated we do committed throughput tiers; partner rev-share is negotiable.
[06:34] Ravi (SableGrid): wanted to confirm: do you run any model compilation or do you require customers to provide compiled kernels?
[06:41] Samir (Redwood): runtime can compile model kernels with our compilation layer; we'll also accept pre-compiled artifacts if you have a preferred stack. often we iterate on kernel selection during onboarding.
[06:58] Lena (SableGrid): great. any open concerns for customers in regulated industries?
[07:04] Maya (Redwood): private control plane + KMS + audit logs generally covers most regulated requirements; for on-prem or air-gapped we have an on-prem package and dedicated support.
[07:16] Priya (SableGrid): ok, let's talk specifics for the benchmark — what inputs do you need?
[07:22] Samir (Redwood): sample prompts, model choice (e.g., Llama-2-70B, Mistral, or open-weights we support), and the expected concurrency profile. we'll also need shell access for the test harness or agent install.
[07:40] Daniel (SableGrid): concurrency: typical ISV customer has 50-200 qps bursts, but avg is much lower; we'll provide a few profiles.
[07:49] Maya (Redwood): perfect. we'll produce a benchmark plan and send over the harness link + step-by-step runbook.
[07:58] Lena (SableGrid): does Redwood do model quantization or do we need to provide quantized models?
[08:04] Samir (Redwood): we can serve quantized models and also have quantization tools; but for some top-accuracy SLAs you might want to test 4-bit vs 8-bit tradeoffs. we'll include recommendations.
[08:18] Maya (Redwood): any questions on partner program mechanics?
[08:22] Priya (SableGrid): just one: are commitments required to be billed monthly or yearly?
[08:29] Maya (Redwood): both options exist; tiered discounts for annual commits. we'll include pricing examples.
[08:36] Daniel (SableGrid): ok looks good. can you share SOC2 and KMS integration docs after?
[08:42] Maya (Redwood): yes — security pack and SOC2 link.
[08:46] Lena (SableGrid): great. last thing — we might want an NDA before sharing some internal topology docs.
[08:52] Maya (Redwood): fine with an NDA; i'll coordinate with legal.
[08:57] Priya (SableGrid): thanks, everyone.
[09:00] Maya (Redwood): recap / next steps: i'll send partner deck and pricing, Samir will share benchmark harness and recommended driver matrix, Lena will loop in infra owner for the deep-dive. schedule deep-dive for next week tentatively.
[09:18] Samir (Redwood): thanks all.

References: partner deck link (placeholder): https://redwood.ai/partner-deck/sablegrid, security pack: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2, benchmark template: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/harness (will be shared via email).

End of transcript.
